name: CoreWC3Workspace
intent: The WC3 unified-workspace app shell: CoreAppSidebar + CoreAppTopBar where every perspective is a sidebar item and each carries its own tabs. Home lands on a card per perspective; Ontology, Lineage, Products, Pipelines, Processes and Analysis are data-bearing surfaces with list/detail drill-in, wizards and dialogs, driven by fixtures extracted from the WC3 ontology-manager prototype.
when: Standing up an admin workspace whose sidebar switches perspectives and whose top tabs switch sections within one
Demonstrating an ontology-backed admin: object/link/action types, lineage, products, pipelines, processes and analysis in one shell
Comparing the Core rendering of the unified-workspace IA against the HTML prototype
whenNot: A single content page rendered inside an existing app shell -> use a content-only template
An org-level admin over projects, roles and users -> use Admin Panel
The WC3 platform application nav (Operations, Resources, Control Panel, …) -> that is a different IA

chooseOver.because: Admin Panel is a three-surface org admin over projects, roles and users. WC3 Workspace is the ontology-backed workspace: seven perspectives, each with its own tabs, drill-in and dialogs.

allowedPlacement: route-level workspace surface that owns the full window

extracted: the 10 perspectives and their rail order from the prototype's PERSPECTIVES array
per-perspective section names from the prototype's own tab arrays (Lineage, Analysis, Products), rail (Ontology), and mode lists (Twin TW_MODES)

lineage.confidence: unset — skeleton only, no held-out eval
notes: skeleton: true — every tab body is an Empty placeholder
follows the Workforce / Safety Manager / Clinic shape: PageContentHeader owns the title and tabs, and Settings is a mode toggled from the header action rather than a tab
the prototype's shell also carries a persona lens, changes drawer, time-machine scrubber, and a bottom context ribbon; none are in this skeleton
Command Center, Schedule, Workforce, Processes, and Pipelines have no top tabs in the prototype — their tabs here are derived from each page's actual sections
